overall: Los Angeles is in the overnight hours with temperatures holding flat at 62.6°F since at least midnight ET — no warming signal yet, which is entirely expected this early. A marine layer is firmly in place (dewpoint 57.2°F, patchy fog noted in the NWS forecast), and light southwest winds around 8 mph are characteristic of coastal onshore flow. The pattern is a classic June Gloom setup with fog burning off mid-morning and only modest afternoon warming.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show tight agreement: ECMWF 68.3°F, HRRR 68.9°F, and NBM 67.0°F all cluster within a 2-degree range, corroborating the official NWS call of a high near 69°F. max_temp_prediction: With strong NWP model agreement in the 67-69°F range, NWS calling for a high near 69°F, and a marine-layer/fog pattern that typically suppresses afternoon highs for coastal LA, today's TMAX should land near 68-69°F. The active alerts (Extreme Heat Warnings, Fire Weather Watches) are all well inland and away from the LA basin, so no heat intrusion is expected. Confidence is moderate-high given tight model clustering, though the fog burn-off timing introduces a modest downside risk if clouds linger longer than expected.
